_readme: correct = the trade key a buyer SHOULD see. also_ok = other defensible keys. Set by human review — this file is the regression baseline.

defects.address: Not disclosed (Sample Report - address field blank
defects.name: No Power Supply to Rear of House

fields.name: No Power Supply to Rear of House
fields.plain_english: The inspector found there appears to be no working power supply to the rear section of the home. This means power points or circuits in that area either aren't connected or aren't functioning correctly.
fields.why_it_matters: A new home must have fully functional electrical installations throughout before handover. This could indicate an incomplete or faulty electrical installation, which is both a safety concern and a livability issue.
fields.location: Hallways and general living spaces - back section of house

defects.address: Not disclosed (Sample Report - address field blank
defects.name: Incorrectly Wired IXL Heat Lamps / Exhaust Fans

fields.name: Incorrectly Wired IXL Heat Lamps / Exhaust Fans
fields.plain_english: In both the bathroom and ensuite, when you turn on the heat lamps the exhaust fan activates at the same time — that's not how it's supposed to work. They should operate independently. Also, in the WC (toilet room), the light switch doesn't engage the light or exhaust fan at all.
fields.why_it_matters: Incorrectly wired fixtures in wet areas are both a functional problem and a potential electrical safety hazard. In a new home this should never be an issue at handover — it's a builder defect.

defects.address: Not disclosed (Sample Report - address field blank
defects.name: Bowed Walls in Multiple Locations

fields.name: Bowed Walls in Multiple Locations
fields.plain_english: The inspector found that internal walls in two separate passages appear to be bowed — meaning they're not straight and flat as they should be. In a brand new home this points to either poor installation of the wall lining (plasterboard) or potential framing issues behind the wall.
fields.why_it_matters: Bowed walls in a new build are unacceptable and indicate substandard workmanship. If caused by framing issues rather than just plasterboard, the fix could be more involved. The builder needs to investigate and rectify.
fields.location: Passage leading to kitchen (left elevation) and passage leading to bathroom (left elevation, bottom section)

defects.address: Not disclosed (Sample Report - address field blank
defects.name: Contaminated Shower Sealants (Both Bathroom and Ensuite)

fields.name: Contaminated Shower Sealants (Both Bathroom and Ensuite)
fields.plain_english: The silicone sealant (the flexible waterproof strip that runs around the edge of the shower) has been contaminated with tile adhesive glue in both wet areas. This compromises the watertight seal — if water gets under that contaminated sealant, it can cause waterproofing failure and leaks into the structure below.
fields.why_it_matters: Shower waterproofing failure is one of the most expensive problems to fix in any home. In a new build, contaminated sealants at handover means the waterproofing is already compromised before anyone has even taken a shower. This needs to be properly stripped back and re-done, not just covered over.
fields.location: Bathroom 1 shower base perimeter and Ensuite 1 shower niche

defects.address: Not disclosed (Sample Report - address field blank
defects.name: Gaps at Top of Shower Tiles (Bathroom and Ensuite)

fields.name: Gaps at Top of Shower Tiles (Bathroom and Ensuite)
fields.plain_english: There are unfilled gaps at the top edge of the tiles in the shower in both the bathroom and ensuite. This means water can get behind the tiles and into the wall, which in a worst case scenario means waterproofing failure and structural damage to the wall framing.
fields.why_it_matters: Water penetration behind shower tiles in a new home can cause timber framing to rot, mould growth in the walls, and expensive remediation work down the track. This must be properly grouted or sealed before handover.
fields.location: Bathroom 1 shower recess and Ensuite 1 shower recess - top edge of tiles

defects.address: Not disclosed (Sample Report - address field blank
defects.name: Entry Door - Multiple Issues (Tight Margins, Poor Fit, Draught Seal, Unpainted Edges, Rusty Striker Plate)

fields.name: Entry Door - Multiple Issues (Tight Margins, Poor Fit, Draught Seal, Unpainted Edges, Rusty Striker Plate)
fields.plain_english: The front door has several problems: the gap around the door is uneven and too tight in places (less than 2mm when it should be consistent), the door doesn't sit flush against the draught seal at the bottom, the draught seals at the bottom aren't properly fitted, the top and bottom edges of the door haven't been painted or sealed (leaving raw timber exposed), and the metal striker plate and screws are already showing rust.
fields.why_it_matters: A poorly fitted entry door lets in draughts, insects, and moisture — plus an unpainted door edge will absorb moisture and potentially warp or rot over time. The rusty striker plate on a brand new home is unacceptable finish quality.

defects.address: Not disclosed (Sample Report - address field blank
defects.name: Gaps Around Doors and Windows Throughout (Energy Rating Risk)

fields.name: Gaps Around Doors and Windows Throughout (Energy Rating Risk)
fields.plain_english: There are gaps at the tops and bottoms of doors and windows throughout the house. The inspector specifically notes this could affect the home's six-star energy rating — meaning the home may not actually perform as efficiently as it was designed and certified to, which affects your heating and cooling bills.
fields.why_it_matters: If the home doesn't meet its energy rating due to sealing defects, it may technically not comply with the National Construction Code. This is a builder obligation to fix before handover.
fields.location: Throughout the home - tops and bottoms of doors and windows

defects.address: Not disclosed (Sample Report - address field blank
defects.name: Garage Internal Access Door Not Sitting Flush with Draught Seal

fields.name: Garage Internal Access Door Not Sitting Flush with Draught Seal
fields.plain_english: The door between the garage and the house doesn't sit properly against its draught seal. This is relevant because the door between a garage and living areas is often required to be fire-rated — a poor fit compromises both fire and carbon monoxide safety.
fields.why_it_matters: The internal garage-to-house door is a fire separation door. It must close tightly and properly to provide the required fire resistance. This is a safety-relevant defect.

defects.address: Not disclosed (Sample Report - address field blank
defects.name: Missing Manhole Cover

fields.name: Missing Manhole Cover
fields.plain_english: The manhole cover (the hatch in the ceiling that gives access to the roof space) is missing entirely, leaving an open hole in the ceiling.
fields.why_it_matters: Pests, vermin and heat loss can occur through an uncovered manhole. It's a straightforward fix but shouldn't be missing on a new home.

defects.address: Not disclosed (Sample Report - address field blank
defects.name: Door Fitting Issues Throughout (Bedroom 1, 2, 3, Bathroom, Ensuite, Laundry)

fields.name: Door Fitting Issues Throughout (Bedroom 1, 2, 3, Bathroom, Ensuite, Laundry)
fields.plain_english: Doors throughout the house have various fitting problems: gaps that are too tight (less than 2mm where they should be consistent), excessive gaps at hinge areas (should be 10-12mm), doors not cut straight at the top, latches that don't properly engage with strike plates, and missing hinges. This is a widespread workmanship issue.
fields.why_it_matters: Doors that don't fit or latch properly are a functional defect. In a new home, every door should be properly hung and adjusted before handover — this level of door problems across the whole house indicates poor attention to detail by the builder's finishing trades.
fields.location: Multiple rooms - Bedroom 1, 2, 3, Bathroom 1 (WC), Ensuite, Laundry, Kitchen pantry

defects.address: Not disclosed (Sample Report - address field blank
defects.name: Missing Laundry Door

fields.name: Missing Laundry Door
fields.plain_english: The laundry door simply hasn't been fitted yet at the time of inspection.
fields.why_it_matters: Incomplete item — must be installed before handover.

defects.address: Not disclosed (Sample Report - address field blank
defects.name: Missing Laundry Cabinet Kick Board

fields.name: Missing Laundry Cabinet Kick Board
fields.plain_english: The decorative panel at the very bottom of the laundry cabinets (the 'kick board' that covers the gap between the cabinet base and the floor) hasn't been installed.
fields.why_it_matters: Cosmetic/incomplete item — exposes the underside of the cabinet to moisture and pests.

defects.address: Not disclosed (Sample Report - address field blank
defects.name: Kitchen Appliances Not Yet Installed

fields.name: Kitchen Appliances Not Yet Installed
fields.plain_english: The oven, range hood, and dishwasher were not installed at the time of inspection.
fields.why_it_matters: These are incomplete items that must be installed and tested before handover. You should ensure these are the exact make and model specified in your contract.

defects.address: Not disclosed (Sample Report - address field blank
defects.name: Kitchen Cabinet Door Alignment Issues and Exposed Plumbing Penetrations

fields.name: Kitchen Cabinet Door Alignment Issues and Exposed Plumbing Penetrations
fields.plain_english: Kitchen cabinet doors don't align properly and have irregular gaps throughout. There are also large exposed gaps around the plumbing pipes under the sink that need to be properly sealed/covered.
fields.why_it_matters: Misaligned kitchen cabinets are a workmanship defect in a new home. The exposed plumbing gaps under the sink can allow moisture, pests and odours into the cabinet space.

defects.address: Not disclosed (Sample Report - address field blank
defects.name: Bedroom 1 Robe - Missing Hanging Rail and Shelf Support

fields.name: Bedroom 1 Robe - Missing Hanging Rail and Shelf Support
fields.plain_english: The hanging rail and its support bracket inside the built-in wardrobe in Bedroom 1 are missing.
fields.why_it_matters: Incomplete item — wardrobe is essentially non-functional without the hanging rail.

defects.address: Not disclosed (Sample Report - address field blank
defects.name: Bathroom - Shower Rail Not Installed

fields.name: Bathroom - Shower Rail Not Installed
fields.plain_english: The shower rail (the bar your shower head slides up and down on) hasn't been installed in the main bathroom.
fields.why_it_matters: Incomplete item — shower is not fully functional.

defects.address: Not disclosed (Sample Report - address field blank
defects.name: Bathroom Shower Tile Grout Pinholes

fields.name: Bathroom Shower Tile Grout Pinholes
fields.plain_english: The tile grout in the shower has numerous small pinholes throughout. Grout that isn't properly filled allows water to seep through, which can undermine the waterproofing membrane behind the tiles.
fields.why_it_matters: Pinholes in shower grout compromise the waterproofing and can lead to leaks into the wall cavity over time.

defects.address: Not disclosed (Sample Report - address field blank
defects.name: Scratched Bathtub

fields.name: Scratched Bathtub
fields.plain_english: The bathtub has visible scratches across various areas — likely caused during construction.
fields.why_it_matters: A brand new bath should be delivered to you in perfect condition. Scratches expose the underlying material and can stain or deteriorate over time.

defects.address: Not disclosed (Sample Report - address field blank
defects.name: Bathroom Vanity Cabinet Hinge Separated

fields.name: Bathroom Vanity Cabinet Hinge Separated
fields.plain_english: The hinge on the top right door of the bathroom vanity has come away from the cabinet body.
fields.why_it_matters: Straightforward fix — cabinet door is non-functional without a properly attached hinge.
fields.location: Bathroom 1 - vanity cabinet, top right door

defects.address: Not disclosed (Sample Report - address field blank
defects.name: Ensuite Cabinet Cracked

fields.name: Ensuite Cabinet Cracked
fields.plain_english: The cabinet body beneath the left basin in the ensuite has a crack in it. On a brand new home this is damage that occurred during construction.
fields.why_it_matters: A cracked cabinet in a new home should be replaced, not left as-is.
fields.location: Ensuite 1 - cabinet below left-hand side basin

defects.address: Not disclosed (Sample Report - address field blank
defects.name: Towel Rail Size Discrepancy in Ensuite

fields.name: Towel Rail Size Discrepancy in Ensuite
fields.plain_english: The towel rail that's been installed is a different (longer) size than what was shown on the approved plans/elevations. The inspector has flagged this and asked for confirmation from the builder about which is correct.
fields.why_it_matters: If the installed item doesn't match the contract specifications, the builder needs to either confirm in writing that the variation is agreed or replace it with the specified item.

defects.address: Not disclosed (Sample Report - address field blank
defects.name: Garage Ceiling/Cornice Line Bowed

fields.name: Garage Ceiling/Cornice Line Bowed
fields.plain_english: The line where the ceiling meets the wall (the cornice) in the garage appears to be bowed rather than straight.
fields.why_it_matters: Poor workmanship in a new home — indicates the ceiling lining or cornice wasn't installed correctly.

defects.address: Not disclosed (Sample Report - address field blank
defects.name: Brickwork - Mortar Smears and Gaps/Holes Throughout Exterior

fields.name: Brickwork - Mortar Smears and Gaps/Holes Throughout Exterior
fields.plain_english: The outside brickwork has two problems: (1) mortar smeared across the face of various bricks that needs to be cleaned off, and (2) gaps and holes in the mortar joints between bricks that need to be filled.
fields.why_it_matters: Mortar smears are mainly cosmetic but difficult to remove once hardened. Gaps in mortar joints allow water to penetrate behind the brickwork, causing moisture problems in walls over time.

defects.address: Not disclosed (Sample Report - address field blank
defects.name: Meter Box Installed Out of Plumb

fields.name: Meter Box Installed Out of Plumb
fields.plain_english: The electricity meter box on the outside of the home isn't vertical — it's been installed on a lean. This is both an aesthetic and workmanship issue.
fields.why_it_matters: The meter box should be properly installed per the electrical authority's requirements. An out-of-plumb meter box may need to be corrected before the electricity authority will accept it.

defects.address: Not disclosed (Sample Report - address field blank
defects.name: Paint Touch-Ups Required Throughout

fields.name: Paint Touch-Ups Required Throughout
fields.plain_english: The inspector noted general paint touch-ups are needed throughout the house. This is common in new builds but should all be completed before you accept handover.
fields.why_it_matters: Standard new home defect — the builder's painter should complete all touch-ups prior to handover at no cost to you.

defects.address: Not disclosed (Sample Report - address field blank
defects.name: Linen/Broom Cupboard - Missing Hinge Screws

fields.name: Linen/Broom Cupboard - Missing Hinge Screws
fields.plain_english: The top left hinge on the linen or broom cupboard door is missing its screws.
fields.why_it_matters: Minor but should be rectified — a hinge without all its screws will eventually fail and the door will drop.
fields.location: Linen/broom cupboard door - top left hinge

defects.address: Not disclosed (Sample Report - address field blank
defects.name: Roof Space Access Limited by Heating Ducts

fields.name: Roof Space Access Limited by Heating Ducts
fields.plain_english: The inspector couldn't fully access the roof space because heating ducts and low-lying areas of the roof blocked physical access.
fields.why_it_matters: This means parts of the roof space structure, insulation and any potential issues could not be inspected. You should ask the builder for documentation confirming insulation installation meets specifications and consider requesting a follow-up inspection if ducts are moved.

fields.name: Bathroom grout and sealant failure
fields.plain_english: The grout and silicone sealant around the tiled wet areas (bath surround, shower) has degraded or gone missing. Water is getting into the gaps every time someone showers or baths.
fields.why_it_matters: Once water gets behind tiles it soaks into the wall framing and subfloor. Left alone this leads to rotting timber framing, mould, and eventually a full bathroom resheet — a job that costs $6,000–$12,000 instead of a few hundred dollars now.

fields.name: Inadequate site drainage
fields.plain_english: Water is pooling against the base of the walls rather than draining away. The site is described as poorly drained, and paving and ground levels are directing water toward the house rather than away from it.
fields.why_it_matters: Persistent moisture against the base of a timber-framed house on stumps is the single biggest driver of termite attack, fungal decay, and rising damp. It's already contributing to the fungal decay found in the weatherboards. Without fixing drainage, any other repairs will fail prematurely.
fields.location: All external areas — perimeter of building

fields.name: Uneven paving falling toward house
fields.plain_english: The external paving is uneven and sloping toward the house rather than away from it. Some sections are also a trip hazard.
fields.why_it_matters: Paving that drains toward the house pushes water into the footings and subfloor — accelerating timber decay and termite risk. The trip hazard also creates a personal injury risk for anyone walking around the property.
fields.location: All external areas — paths and paved areas around building perimeter

fields.name: Rusted shed roof sheets
fields.plain_english: The corrugated iron roof sheets on the shed are heavily rusted and corroding through. Photos show rust across the entire roof surface and holes forming at the sheet overlaps.
fields.why_it_matters: A rusted-through roof lets water in, which will rot the shed's timber framing and any contents stored inside. The shed is also a termite risk if moisture accumulates in the timber structure beneath.

fields.name: Deteriorated external paint — widespread
fields.plain_english: The external paint is peeling, cracking, and missing across large sections of the weatherboards, fascias, and window frames. Bare timber is exposed in multiple locations.
fields.why_it_matters: On an 80-year-old timber weatherboard house, paint is the primary protection against moisture and rot. Bare timber absorbs water, swells, cracks, and decays — and the pest report has already confirmed fungal decay is present in the weatherboards. Every month without paint accelerates the rot.
fields.location: All external areas — weatherboards, fascias, window frames, verandah

fields.name: Leaning brick pier — veranda subsidence
fields.plain_english: One of the decorative brick piers supporting the front veranda is leaning considerably. This is a structural concern that needs a structural engineer to assess before you can know how serious it is.
fields.why_it_matters: A leaning pier can indicate foundation movement, soil subsidence, or mortar failure. If the pier is load-bearing for the veranda roof, it could collapse. At minimum it needs rebuilding; at worst it signals broader foundation movement that could be expensive to address.
fields.location: Front left corner of veranda — external

fields.name: Leaking kitchen tap
fields.plain_english: The kitchen tap is dripping or leaking. A straightforward plumbing repair.
fields.why_it_matters: Ongoing water waste and potential for water damage under the sink if the leak worsens.

fields.name: Moving/squeaky floorboards
fields.plain_english: The floorboards move and creak underfoot, indicating they've come loose from the joists beneath.
fields.why_it_matters: Squeaky floors are usually a nuisance rather than a structural issue, but in a house with known termite workings and wood borer in the Baltic pine floors, any floor movement warrants closer inspection of the subfloor once access is available.

fields.name: Loose cabinet hinges — bathroom
fields.plain_english: Several cupboard door hinges have come loose from their fixings. Doors are sagging or not closing properly.
fields.why_it_matters: Cosmetic and functional nuisance only. Easy handyman fix.

fields.name: Shower recess components — general condition
fields.plain_english: The shower recess components (screen, base, seals) were noted as requiring attention. Given the grout and sealant failure already flagged as a major defect, the shower should be assessed for leaks before purchase.
fields.why_it_matters: A leaking shower can cause significant hidden damage to the subfloor and wall framing in a timber-framed house.

fields.name: Deteriorated fencing
fields.plain_english: Sections of the timber paling fencing around the property have rotted and deteriorated due to age and weather exposure.
fields.why_it_matters: Deteriorated fencing is a security and privacy issue. Rotting timber in contact with the ground is also a termite attractant.

fields.name: Loose front balustrade/handrail
fields.plain_english: The front handrail to the verandah is loose and not fixed securely.
fields.why_it_matters: A loose handrail is a fall risk, particularly for children or elderly visitors. Should be fixed promptly.

fields.name: Floors out of level — throughout
fields.plain_english: The internal floors are noticeably out of level in multiple rooms. The inspector's photos show a spirit level with a significant gap across multiple rooms.
fields.why_it_matters: Some floor movement is expected in an 80-year-old stumped house. However, combined with the subfloor access limitations and the termite/borer findings, this warrants a proper subfloor inspection once access is available. If stumps have failed or been damaged by pests, restumping could be a significant cost.

fields.name: Hairline cracks in plaster lining
fields.plain_english: Hairline cracks are visible in the plaster walls and ceilings throughout the house. The inspector describes these as cosmetic and common in a house of this age.
fields.why_it_matters: Hairline cracks alone are cosmetic. However, if they widen or new ones appear after you move in, it could indicate ongoing foundation movement — worth monitoring.
fields.location: All internal areas — walls and ceilings

fields.name: Internal paint touch-ups required
fields.plain_english: Various internal walls and surfaces need paint touch-ups to restore appearance.
fields.why_it_matters: Cosmetic only.

defects.name: Doors and windows difficult to operate

fields.name: Doors and windows difficult to operate
fields.plain_english: Multiple doors and windows are binding, jamming, or sticking and won't open or close smoothly.
fields.why_it_matters: In a house with out-of-level floors, sticking doors and windows can be a symptom of ongoing foundation movement. Most cases in an old house are just seasonal timber swelling, but worth monitoring alongside the floor levels.

defects.name: Loose roof frame purlin strut — non-compliant alteration

fields.name: Loose roof frame purlin strut — non-compliant alteration
fields.plain_english: Someone has altered the roof framing structure and a purlin strut (a timber brace that supports the roof) is now loose. The modifications don't comply with current building standards and a building permit was required but may not have been obtained.
fields.why_it_matters: A loose purlin strut reduces the structural integrity of the roof frame. You should check with Maribyrnong Council whether a building permit was issued for this work. If not, you may need to retrospectively approve or rectify it.

defects.name: Termite workings and damage — internal areas

fields.name: Termite workings and damage — internal areas
fields.plain_english: Evidence of past termite workings and/or damage was found inside the house. The extent was undetermined due to obstructions (wall linings, floor coverings). No live termites were found on the day, but the inspector notes that absence of live termites doesn't mean the colony is gone.
fields.why_it_matters: Termite damage can be hidden behind wall linings and under floors. The full extent is unknown until an invasive inspection is done. Structural framing damage from termites can cost $8,000–$25,000+ to repair. This is the single biggest financial unknown in this report.

fields.name: Termite workings and damage — roofspace
fields.plain_english: Termite damage was found in the roof timbers. The damage appeared localised but the full extent couldn't be determined. A licensed builder needs to assess whether any structural roof members have been compromised.
fields.why_it_matters: Roof framing damaged by termites can fail under load. Repair costs depend on how many members are affected — could range from a few thousand dollars to a full roof reframe.

fields.name: Fungal decay — weatherboards and fascias (widespread)
fields.plain_english: The timber weatherboards and fascias have widespread fungal decay (rot). The inspector probed the timber and it tested as decayed. This is beyond just peeling paint — the timber itself is breaking down.
fields.why_it_matters: Decayed weatherboards and fascias need to be replaced, not just repainted. If left, the rot spreads into the structural wall framing behind. Given the extent described as 'widespread', this is a significant repair job.
fields.location: All external areas — weatherboards and fascias

defects.name: Wood borer (furniture beetle) — Baltic pine flooring throughout

fields.name: Wood borer (furniture beetle) — Baltic pine flooring throughout
fields.plain_english: The Baltic pine floorboards throughout the house have widespread wood borer (furniture beetle, Anobium punctatum) damage. The inspector couldn't confirm if the attack is still active without breaking open the timber, but says it should be treated as active unless proven otherwise.
fields.why_it_matters: Wood borer weakens floorboards over time. Widespread attack means the floors may need chemical treatment and potentially replacement of the most affected boards. Baltic pine is particularly susceptible and replacement with non-susceptible timber is the most effective fix.
fields.location: All internal areas — Baltic pine floorboards

fields.name: No termite management system installed
fields.plain_english: There is no termite barrier or management system protecting this property — no chemical barrier, no baiting system, nothing. There's no notice in the switchboard indicating any previous treatment either.
fields.why_it_matters: An unprotected 80-year-old timber house in Melbourne is extremely vulnerable to termite attack. Given that termite workings have already been found, installing a management system is not optional — it's essential. This needs to happen immediately after purchase.

fields.name: Inadequate subfloor ventilation
fields.plain_english: The ventilation under the house is inadequate. There aren't enough vents to keep the subfloor dry and well-aired.
fields.why_it_matters: Poor subfloor ventilation creates the damp, humid conditions that termites and fungal decay thrive in. It's a direct contributor to the rot and pest issues already found. Fixing ventilation is a prerequisite for any other subfloor repairs to last.

fields.name: Excessive moisture — external areas
fields.plain_english: Excessive moisture was detected around the external perimeter of the house, linked to poor drainage, leaking plumbing connections, and vegetation against the walls.
fields.why_it_matters: Moisture is the root cause of both the fungal decay and the termite conducive conditions. Until the moisture sources are fixed, pest and decay problems will keep recurring.

fields.name: Termite inspection zones breached — widespread
fields.plain_english: The areas around the base of the house that should be kept clear so termites can be spotted (called inspection zones) are blocked by paving, gardens, earth, vegetation, decking, and pipework on all four sides of the house. Termites could be entering the house undetected right now.
fields.why_it_matters: When inspection zones are blocked, termites can travel from the soil into the house walls without anyone seeing them. This is a major risk factor and needs to be cleared as a priority.
fields.location: All external areas — front, rear, both sides

defects.address: Lot 2 No. 2 Commerce Court, Kilmore, VIC
defects.name: Drummy and moving floor tiles — hallway and stair top

fields.name: Drummy and moving floor tiles — hallway and stair top
fields.plain_english: When you tap or walk on these tiles, they sound hollow (that's what 'drummy' means) and they're actually moving underfoot — you can see this because the grout joints are already cracking from the movement. Under Australian Standard AS 3958.1, more than 20% hollow-sounding tiles is considered suspect and a defect. The inspector suspects the tiles weren't bedded properly — likely the tiler didn't use the right notched trowel technique or didn't 'butter' the back of the tiles as required for larger format tiles.
fields.why_it_matters: Moving tiles on a staircase landing and hallway are a trip and slip risk over time as the tiles continue to crack and lift. Left unaddressed, the tiles will eventually fail completely, requiring a much larger and more disruptive re-tiling job. The builder should investigate by removing a tile or two to confirm the bonding method used, then rectify — which may mean lifting and re-laying the affected area. This should be addressed before you sign off practical completion.
fields.location: Hallway to Bedroom 4 and top of stairs

defects.address: Lot 2 No. 2 Commerce Court, Kilmore, VIC
defects.name: Damaged galvanised coating on window and door lintels

fields.name: Damaged galvanised coating on window and door lintels
fields.plain_english: The metal lintels (the horizontal steel beams that sit above your windows and doors to carry the brickwork load) have had their protective zinc/galvanised coating damaged by the acid wash used to clean the brickwork during construction. This has been flagged in every inspection since September 2024 — three inspections — and still hasn't been fixed.
fields.why_it_matters: Without the protective coating, the steel lintels will rust. Rust expands as it forms, which can crack and push out the brickwork above your windows and doors over time. This is a long-term durability issue. The builder needs to properly clean the affected lintels and apply an appropriate rust-inhibiting paint or coating. The fact this has been outstanding since September 2024 across three inspections is a concern — include it prominently in your rectification letter.
fields.location: Window and door lintels — external (multiple locations)

defects.address: Lot 2 No. 2 Commerce Court, Kilmore, VIC
defects.name: Front entry door seal not sealing properly

fields.name: Front entry door seal not sealing properly
fields.plain_english: The weatherseal on the front door isn't doing its job — air and potentially water can get in around the door when it's closed. The builder has already agreed to replace the door, so this should be a straightforward resolution.
fields.why_it_matters: Draughts, energy inefficiency, and potential water ingress in heavy rain. Builder has agreed to replace the door — confirm this is completed before sign-off.

defects.address: Lot 2 No. 2 Commerce Court, Kilmore, VIC
defects.name: Squeaking door hinges — multiple doors

fields.name: Squeaking door hinges — multiple doors
fields.plain_english: Several door hinges squeak and need adjustment. This has been flagged since September 2024 and remains unaddressed across three inspections.
fields.why_it_matters: A minor annoyance now, but the fact it's been on the list since September 2024 without being fixed reflects a pattern of the builder not following through on small items. Include it in the rectification letter to ensure it gets done.
fields.location: Ensuite door (Bed 1), WC, Powder Room (PDR), Bed 3

defects.address: Lot 2 No. 2 Commerce Court, Kilmore, VIC
defects.name: Sliding screen and glass doors not functioning smoothly

fields.name: Sliding screen and glass doors not functioning smoothly
fields.plain_english: All sliding doors — including the screen door and the glass sliding doors — are stiff and don't slide smoothly. They need to be serviced and adjusted. This has been flagged since September 2024.
fields.why_it_matters: Stiff sliding doors are a daily frustration and can damage the door tracks and rollers over time if not adjusted. The builder should service all sliding doors before handover.
fields.location: Verandah sliding screen door and all sliding glass doors throughout

defects.address: Lot 2 No. 2 Commerce Court, Kilmore, VIC
defects.name: Kitchen sliding window lock not functioning correctly

fields.name: Kitchen sliding window lock not functioning correctly
fields.plain_english: The lock on the kitchen sliding window doesn't work properly. It needs to be serviced or replaced so it locks securely.
fields.why_it_matters: A window that doesn't lock properly is a security issue and may affect your home insurance. The builder should rectify before sign-off.

defects.address: Lot 2 No. 2 Commerce Court, Kilmore, VIC
defects.name: Shower floor tile caulk incomplete and cracked grout at skirting tile

fields.name: Shower floor tile caulk incomplete and cracked grout at skirting tile
fields.plain_english: The caulking (flexible waterproof sealant) between the floor tiles in the shower hasn't been fully applied, and there's a crack in the grout at the skirting tile next to the shower base. The main shower base levelling issue from the previous report has been fixed, but these two sub-items remain outstanding.
fields.why_it_matters: Incomplete caulking and cracked grout in a shower are potential water ingress points. Water getting under tiles in a wet area can cause waterproofing failure, tile delamination, and structural damage to the substrate over time. The builder should complete the caulking and re-grout the cracked skirting tile joint before sign-off.

defects.address: Lot 2 No. 2 Commerce Court, Kilmore, VIC
defects.name: Bath window — rough edges, missing paint, rust deposits, ill-fitting fly screen

fields.name: Bath window — rough edges, missing paint, rust deposits, ill-fitting fly screen
fields.plain_english: When the builder repaired this window (from a previous inspection finding), they left the window frame with rough unfinished edges and didn't touch up the paint. There are also rust deposits sitting in the bottom track that weren't cleaned up. On top of that, the fly wire screen isn't sitting properly in the frame.
fields.why_it_matters: Rust left in the track will continue to corrode and can stain tiles and grout. Rough edges and missing paint are below the standard you contracted for. The fly screen not fitting properly means insects can get in. All three sub-items should be on the rectification list.

defects.address: Lot 2 No. 2 Commerce Court, Kilmore, VIC
defects.name: Linen cupboard door catches not adjusted — right side

fields.name: Linen cupboard door catches not adjusted — right side
fields.plain_english: The magnetic or roller catches on the right-side linen door don't work properly — the door doesn't close easily. This has been flagged since September 2024 and remains unaddressed.
fields.why_it_matters: Minor daily annoyance. Simple adjustment by the builder's carpenter. The fact it's been on the list since September 2024 is the main concern — make sure it's captured in the rectification letter.

defects.name: Sagging Roof Structure — Possible Framing Failure

fields.name: Sagging Roof Structure — Possible Framing Failure
fields.plain_english: The roof tiles and fascia at the front of the house are visibly sagging. The inspector couldn't get into the roof space to check the timber frame underneath, but the sagging strongly suggests the structural timber members holding the roof up have deteriorated or moved. Think of it like a bookshelf bowing in the middle — the shelves (tiles) are drooping because the supports underneath are failing.
fields.why_it_matters: If the roof framing is deteriorating, it will continue to worsen and could eventually lead to partial roof collapse. Water will also be getting in through the displaced tiles, causing further damage to ceilings, walls and the subfloor below. This is the single most expensive and serious structural item in the report.
fields.location: Front elevation roof — hip tiles, adjacent roof tiles and fascia lining

defects.name: Active Termites (Coptotermes) On Site — No Termite Management System

fields.name: Active Termites (Coptotermes) On Site — No Termite Management System
fields.plain_english: Live termites of the species Coptotermes were found actively feeding in tree stumps in the backyard. Coptotermes are the most destructive termite species in Australia — they are responsible for the majority of serious structural damage to homes. There is zero evidence that any termite barrier or treatment has ever been installed at this property: no drill holes, no treatment tags, no durable notice, nothing. The subfloor and roof void — the two places termites most commonly attack — could not be inspected. The inspector has rated the property HIGH risk and recommends inspections every 6 months.
fields.why_it_matters: With live Coptotermes metres from the house, no barrier protection, and two key areas (subfloor and roof void) completely uninspected, there is a real and present risk that termites have already entered the structure. Concealed termite damage to floor joists, bearers, wall frames or roof timbers could be extensive and would only be revealed by invasive investigation. Treatment alone costs $1,500–$3,500; if structural timber damage is found, repair costs could be $20,000–$80,000+.
fields.location: Rear garden — tree stumps; termite workings and damage also observed to multiple tree stumps

defects.name: Suspected Asbestos — Boundary Fence and Shed Roof

fields.name: Suspected Asbestos — Boundary Fence and Shed Roof
fields.plain_english: The inspector observed that the boundary fence and the roof sheeting on the shed look visually consistent with asbestos cement sheeting — the kind commonly used in WA homes built before the mid-1980s. Some of this material is damaged and deteriorating. No lab testing was done to confirm it, but given the property's age (~50 years), asbestos cement sheeting is very likely. Damaged asbestos is a health hazard because it can release fibres into the air.
fields.why_it_matters: Damaged asbestos sheeting must be managed or removed by a licensed asbestos removalist in accordance with WA regulations. You cannot simply paint over cracked or broken asbestos sheeting. If you disturb it during any renovation or landscaping work without knowing it's there, you risk serious health consequences. An asbestos assessment and safe removal/encapsulation is required.
fields.location: Boundary fence and shed roof cover

defects.name: Extensive Brickwork Cracking at Garage — Corroding Steel Lintel

fields.name: Extensive Brickwork Cracking at Garage — Corroding Steel Lintel
fields.plain_english: There is extensive cracking in the brickwork around the garage door. The inspector believes this is caused by the steel beam (called a lintel) above the garage door rusting and expanding — when steel rusts, it swells and pushes the bricks apart. This is a progressive problem: the more the steel rusts, the more the bricks crack and move.
fields.why_it_matters: If left unaddressed, the masonry above the garage door will continue to deteriorate and could become structurally unsafe. Rectification involves removing the affected brickwork, replacing the corroded lintel with a new one, and rebuilding the brickwork — a significant and disruptive job.
fields.location: Brickwork surrounding the garage door opening

fields.name: Cracking to Exterior Brickwork
fields.plain_english: Cracking was observed in the exterior brick walls at various points around the property. The inspector considers this consistent with normal movement for a 50-year-old double brick home, but notes it cannot be ruled out as ongoing movement.
fields.why_it_matters: Most of this cracking is likely cosmetic or minor settlement, but it should be monitored. If cracks widen or new ones appear, a structural engineer should assess whether there is an underlying foundation issue.
fields.location: Multiple locations around the exterior of the building

defects.name: Cracking to Interior Brickwork — Living Room

fields.name: Cracking to Interior Brickwork — Living Room
fields.plain_english: Step cracking (diagonal cracking that follows the mortar joints in a staircase pattern) was observed on an internal brick wall near the living room window. This pattern is typically associated with differential settlement — one part of the foundation moving slightly differently to another.
fields.why_it_matters: Step cracking in internal brickwork warrants monitoring. If it progresses, it could indicate a more serious foundation movement issue that would require engineering assessment.
fields.location: Internal wall adjacent to window in the living room

fields.name: Bouncy and Creaky Interior Floors
fields.plain_english: Sections of the floor feel springy and creak when you walk on them. Because the inspector couldn't access the subfloor, the cause is unknown — it could be as simple as loose floorboards, or as serious as deteriorated stumps, bearers or joists underneath. Given the confirmed presence of live termites on site and no termite barrier, this is a significant unknown.
fields.why_it_matters: Bouncy floors in a property with active termites and no subfloor access is a red flag. The subfloor must be properly inspected before you can understand whether this is a minor maintenance issue or a major structural problem. Do not proceed without a subfloor inspection.

defects.name: Elevated Moisture — Rear of Bathroom / Adjoining Cupboard

fields.name: Elevated Moisture — Rear of Bathroom / Adjoining Cupboard
fields.plain_english: The inspector's moisture meter detected elevated moisture levels in the wall at the back of the bathroom cupboard, and paint and plaster were visibly deteriorating in that area. The source of the moisture couldn't be identified — it could be a leaking pipe, shower waterproofing failure, or condensation.
fields.why_it_matters: Ongoing moisture in a wall creates ideal conditions for mould growth, timber decay, and termite activity. The source needs to be found and fixed by a plumber or builder. If it's a waterproofing failure behind the shower, the tiles may need to come off to fix it properly.
fields.location: Rear of shared bathroom — adjoining cupboard wall

defects.name: Mould Growth — Bedroom Ceiling and Bathroom

fields.name: Mould Growth — Bedroom Ceiling and Bathroom
fields.plain_english: Mould was found growing on the ceiling in a bedroom and in the bathroom. This is typically caused by poor ventilation and/or moisture getting in from above or from condensation.
fields.why_it_matters: Mould can cause health issues, particularly for people with respiratory conditions. It also indicates an underlying moisture problem that needs to be addressed. The source (roof leak, condensation, poor ventilation) needs to be identified and fixed.
fields.location: Ceiling lining of a bedroom and the bathroom

defects.name: Inadequate Site Drainage — Downpipes Discharging to Ground

fields.name: Inadequate Site Drainage — Downpipes Discharging to Ground
fields.plain_english: The roof downpipes are dumping water directly onto the ground next to the house rather than connecting to soakwells or a proper stormwater system. This means every time it rains, water pools around the base of the walls and under the house.
fields.why_it_matters: Water pooling around the base of the house is one of the biggest contributors to termite activity, rising damp, and subfloor moisture problems. Given the active termites already on site, this is particularly concerning and should be rectified promptly.

fields.name: Rusting Carport Structure
fields.plain_english: Rusting was observed to the carport structure. The photos show significant rust and deterioration to the carport framing and fascia.
fields.why_it_matters: Rusted structural steel in a carport can become unsafe over time. The extent of the rust needs to be assessed — surface rust can be treated, but if the steel is structurally compromised it may need replacement.

fields.name: Blocked Weepholes
fields.plain_english: Weepholes are small gaps left in the bottom row of brickwork to let moisture escape from inside the wall cavity and to allow ventilation. These were found to be blocked — likely by mulch, soil or landscaping materials piled up against the walls.
fields.why_it_matters: Blocked weepholes trap moisture inside the wall cavity and also create a concealed entry point for termites. They need to be cleared and the garden beds/mulch pulled back from the base of the walls.

defects.name: Live Coptotermes Termites — Active Colony on Site

fields.name: Live Coptotermes Termites — Active Colony on Site
fields.plain_english: Live termites of the species Coptotermes were confirmed active in tree stumps in the backyard. Coptotermes are the most destructive termite species in Australia — they build large underground colonies and can silently eat through the structural timber of a house from the inside out. The nest was not located, meaning the colony could be anywhere — including under the house.
fields.location: Tree stumps in the rear garden

fields.name: Historical Termite Workings — Tree Stumps
fields.plain_english: In addition to the live termites, there is evidence of past termite activity (old workings and damage) in several tree stumps. This confirms the property has had a termite problem for some time.
fields.location: Multiple tree stumps in the rear garden

defects.name: No Termite Management System — No Durable Notice

fields.name: No Termite Management System — No Durable Notice
fields.plain_english: There is absolutely no evidence that any termite protection has ever been installed at this property. No chemical barrier, no physical barrier, no bait stations, no treatment records, no durable notice in the meter box. For a 50-year-old Perth home with active Coptotermes on site, this is extremely concerning.
